title: Acceptance thresholds: ground-station geometry of the core versus JPL Horizons
rule: Written and committed together with cases.json before any of these Horizons responses was fetched and before the station code of the core existed. Not edited afterwards. If a comparison exceeds a threshold, the cause is found and reported; the threshold stays.
what_is_checked: The two conditions of a direct link between a lunar site and a ground station: (a) how high the lunar site stands above the station's horizon (Earth end), (b) where the station appears in the sky of the lunar site (Moon end). No terrain on either side.

earth_end_direction_arcsec_max.definition: Largest great-circle angle between the apparent direction of the lunar site seen from the station computed by the core (observer at the station, light time and stellar aberration, station's topocentric frame of the NAIF kernel) and the airless apparent azimuth and elevation printed by Horizons for the same station.

moon_end_direction_arcsec_max.definition: Largest great-circle angle between the apparent direction of the station seen from the lunar site computed by the core (observer at the site) and the azimuth and elevation printed by Horizons for a target at the station's geodetic coordinates.

fast_path_earth_end_deg_max.definition: Largest difference in the elevation of the lunar site at the station between the fast path used for the windows (station position and zenith tabulated every 10 minutes relative to the Moon's centre, both ends evaluated at one instant) and Horizons.
fast_path_earth_end_deg_max.why_this_value: The fast path ignores the light time between the two ends (at most 1.4 s); the Earth turns 15.04 arcsec per second, so the elevation at the station can differ by up to 21 arcsec. The threshold is twice that.

fast_path_moon_end_arcsec_max.definition: Largest great-circle angle between the direction of the station seen from the lunar site through the fast path and Horizons.

station_masks.note: Not thresholds: the elevation limits the windows use, recorded here with their source so that they are fixed before any window is computed.
station_masks.source: DSN Telecommunications Link Design Handbook 810-005, module 301 'Coverage and Geometry', Rev. N, 15 April 2022, https://deepspace.jpl.nasa.gov/dsndocs/810-005/301/301N.pdf: generic elevation limits of 6.0 degrees for receive and 10.0 degrees for low-power transmit; the mechanical elevation limit is approximately six degrees.
